title: Calibration-driven kernel router for mixed-precision inference (FP16/FP8/INT8)
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Implement a runtime kernel routing component that selects between FP16, FP8, and INT8 execution paths using per-model and per-layer quantization profiles produced by calibration workflows, while enforcing accuracy guards and cost/latency trade-offs. The router must be able to: load calibration metadata (scale/zero-point, per-channel vs per-tensor, layer sensitivity), consult a lightweight cost model (latency + token-cost), and dispatch requests to the best kernel variant. It should also support graceful fallbacks when calibration confidence is low or accuracy regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Router can read and interpret quantization profile files generated by the calibration pipeline (schema v1)
Per-layer routing decisions are logged with telemetry (chosen precision, expected latency, expected quality delta)
End-to-end latency regression for representative small-chat workload is <= 5% compared to FP16 baseline when routing to faster precision paths
Accuracy regression (measured with our calibration validation suite) is within defined thresholds: <= 0.5% average token-level metric drop on eval set or triggers automatic fallback
Fallback flow correctly routes to alternate kernel (FP16 or FP8->FP16) when calibration confidence flag is low or when runtime validation signals a quality regression
Unit and integration tests cover: profile parsing, cost-model scoring, routing decision determinism, fallback triggers, and telemetry emission
planned_work: Design schema extension for quantization profile: include per-layer sensitivity score, calibration confidence, and histogram summaries
Build lightweight cost model used by router (cost per token vs expected latency for each kernel variant)
Implement profile loader and cache in runtime with TTL and invalidation hooks
Implement router abstraction: plugin points for kernel descriptors, routing heuristics, and fallback policies
Add runtime telemetry: routing decisions, observed latency, per-request quality probe results
Integrate runtime unit tests and end-to-end validation harness with calibration validation suite
Prepare canary rollout plan and A/B test against FP16 baseline with automatic rollback on quality regressions
notes: Background: existing quant profiles (ENG-16203, ENG-11958) provide calibration outputs but we currently lack a high-level decision layer in the runtime to select kernels per-request.
We must avoid per-token re-evaluation in hot paths; routing should be computed at request start and cached across KV-cache hits for the same model/sequence-length bucket.
Calibration confidence heuristic idea: combine per-layer sensitivity, aggregate KL-divergence estimate, and sample-size-adjusted variance to produce a single confidence score (0..1).

Cost model will initially be linear combination: alpha*latency + beta*cost, tunable via feature flags for experiments. Default prioritizes latency for low-p99 SLO customers and cost for background batch workloads.
Schema v1 must be backwards compatible with current calibration outputs. If missing fields, router should assume conservative defaults (prefer FP16).
Consider GPU-specific kernel availability: some devices may not have FP8 kernels compiled for long sequence lengths; router must consult device capability registry before selection.
